claims.text: POL-NS-01 is conjunctive, and limb (b) fails on the driver's own telemetry. The derived driver track never comes closer than 881.64 m to the T4 pickup pin across 79 fixes, while the derived arrival block records 0 qualifying in-radius fixes against the 150 m arrival radius that the fee_schedule sets for the AIRPORT zone class. A driver who never entered the arrival radius did not arrive at the pickup point.

Limb (c) fails independently of proximity. The longest continuous in-geofence run in the derived arrival block is 0.0 seconds, measured from the (non-existent) first qualifying in-geofence fix, against a required continuous dwell of 480 seconds for an AIRPORT pickup. The required hold was never begun, let alone completed.

Limb (d) fails on the trip record's own terms. The trip was cancelled by the rider with cancellation_reason_code RIDER_CHANGED_MIND, which is none of the three codes limb (d) recognises (RIDER_NO_SHOW, RIDER_UNREACHABLE, EXCESSIVE_WAIT), and the record shows no boarding event. Three of the four POL-NS-01 conditions therefore fail, and the fee is not chargeable under this clause.

The 'arrived' marker struck at 16:14:40 is FALSE under POL-NS-05: at the arrival timestamp the driver's trace places him more than 300 m from the pickup pin — his closest approach on the entire trip is 881.64 m, so he was more than 300 m away at every instant of the attempt. Because no qualifying in-geofence fix exists anywhere in the trip, POL-NS-05(ii) applies: the cancellation fee is refunded in full, no driver compensation is payable, and the trip should be recorded as a false-arrival event in the ruling's referrals list.

The driver's own words in the chat log confirm the marker was false. Asked at 16:15:40 'where are you? I'm at the T4 pickup door', he answered 'not yet' at 16:16:20 — one minute and forty seconds AFTER he had pressed 'arrived' — and his filed statement says only that he pressed arrived 'so she'd know I was near'. A driver who answers 'not yet' has not arrived; POL-NS-02 is not satisfied and the contested SGD 6.00 is refundable in full. The fare line itself reconciles at SGD 6.00 (the greater of the AIRPORT zone-class fee and the RYDE_X tier fee), so this is a chargeability failure, not an arithmetic one, and the refund is the whole SGD 6.00.

The effective in-geofence dwell is 0 seconds against the 480-second AIRPORT minimum, a shortfall of 480 seconds, so POL-NS-06 refunds the cancellation fee in full whether or not the rider was present and expressly provides that no driver compensation is payable. The driver cannot rescue the shortfall by accumulating dwell across intervals under POL-NS-06(i): the derived arrival block records that limb (i) is unavailable because EV-ADVIS-00614-01 is MISSING — weight 0.0, no advisory covers the pickup road in this window — and that absence is itself citable. I disclose that this cited artifact carries weight 0.0; the deciding dwell figure does not rest on it but on the GPS trace at full weight.

The driver's 'holding area' account does not turn this into a wrong-entrance case. POL-NS-03 applies only where the driver was stationary outside the arrival radius but within 400 m of the pickup pin; his own trace places him between 881.64 m and 1,467.21 m away throughout the attempt, outside that ceiling, so POL-NS-03 is not engaged at all and nothing in it displaces the full refund that POL-NS-02 and POL-NS-06 give the rider.

No driver compensation can be ordered on these facts. POL-NS-07 pays only where POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full and no clause from POL-NS-03 to POL-NS-06 displaces it; here POL-NS-01 fails on limbs (b), (c) and (d), and POL-NS-05 and POL-NS-06 displace it and state in terms that no compensation is payable. There is accordingly no driver-side cost for the rider to fund and no basis for leaving the charge in place.

The rider was at the pin and coordinating, not absent: the rider track holds 67 fixes all within 20.23 m of the pickup pin, well inside the 200 m AIRPORT rider-presence radius, and she wrote 'where are you? I'm at the T4 pickup door'. I do not rely on POL-NS-04 for the refund — its limb (b) is not met, because the driver did reply in the chat within 120 seconds (rider's message 16:15:40, driver's reply 16:16:20) — and I say so rather than stretch it. The refund rests on POL-NS-02, POL-NS-05 and POL-NS-06, none of which depends on the rider's conduct.

claims.text: The trip record contains a driver 'arrived' event for this trip at 16:14:40, so limb (a) of POL-NS-01 - the requirement that the trip_record contain an 'arrived' event for the trip - is satisfied on the face of the record.

The cancellation fee the ledger actually took is the correct figure for this trip and cannot be impeached on amount: this is an AIRPORT zone-class pickup, the zone-class fee is SGD 6.00 and the RYDE_X vehicle-tier fee is SGD 4.00, and the greater of the two under the fee_schedule resolution rule - SGD 6.00 - is exactly what fare_breakdown.cancellation_fee records, so there is no POL-NS-08(d) fare defect available to the rider.

POL-NS-04 cannot exonerate the rider: her locating message ('where are you? I'm at the T4 pickup door') was sent at 16:15:40 and the driver posted a reply at 16:16:20, forty seconds later and well inside the 120-second window, so limb (b) of POL-NS-04 fails and that rider-exonerating route is closed on the chat log itself.

There is no fee-farming pattern to hold against the driver, and the anti-farming check under POL-NS-07 does not trip: driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 2 and driver_profile.completed_trips_30d is 95, a ratio of 0.021 against a 0.08 gate, and both limbs of that test are required.

The rider's assertion that the driver 'wanted a surcharge and thought I was a tourist' is not supported anywhere in the record: the chat log is complete and unredacted at three messages, matching trip_record.chat_message_count of 3, and the driver's only substantive line - 'if wait too long app charge you not me' - states the platform's own wait rule rather than demanding anything, so that element of the claim is unsupported and cannot carry an adverse finding under POL-GEN-03.

ruling.explanation:
Rider — the SGD 6.00 cancellation fee is refunded to you in full. Driver — the charge does not stand and no compensation is payable to you on this trip.

ARRIVAL. The trip record carries an 'arrived' tap at 16:14:40 (EV-TRIP-00614). The GPS trace for this trip (EV-GPS-00614, 79 fixes at 10-second cadence, 100% coverage, weight 1.0) never places the vehicle closer than 881.64 m to the T4 pickup pin at any instant of the attempt (mean 951.64 m, maximum 1,467.21 m), and it records 0 qualifying in-radius fixes against the 150 m arrival radius the fee schedule sets for the AIRPORT zone class. The tap is therefore a FALSE marker under POL-NS-05: you were more than 300 m from the pin when you pressed it.

CHARGEABILITY. POL-NS-01 is conjunctive and three limbs fail. Limb (b) fails under POL-NS-02 — no qualifying in-radius fix at any point. Limb (c) fails under POL-NS-06 — the longest continuous in-geofence run is 0.0 seconds against the 480 seconds required for an AIRPORT pickup, a shortfall of 480 seconds; limb (i) accumulation is unavailable because EV-ADVIS-00614-01 is MISSING (weight 0.0) and POL-NS-06(i) requires a present, populated advisory. Limb (d) fails because the trip was terminated by the rider with cancellation_reason_code RIDER_CHANGED_MIND, which is not one of the three codes that limb recognises, and no boarding event is recorded.

YOUR ACCOUNT. Your 'holding area' explanation was considered. POL-NS-03 (wrong entrance / wrong block) requires you to have been stationary within 400 m of the pin; your own trace puts you between 881.64 m and 1,467.21 m away throughout, so that clause is not engaged and nothing in it displaces the refund. Your chat line 'not yet', sent 1 min 40 s after the tap, is consistent with the trace. POL-NS-04 does not apply either way — you did reply within 120 seconds (rider 16:15:40, driver 16:16:20) — and the rider does not rely on it.

COMPENSATION. None is payable. POL-NS-07 pays only where POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full, and here it fails on three limbs. The anti-farming check does not trip: driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 2 against 95 completed trips in 30 days, a ratio of 0.021, below both the 4-count and the 0.08-rate gates (both limbs required).

AMOUNT. SGD 6.00 is the sum actually charged (EV-FARE-00614: total_charged 6.00, payment_status CHARGED) and it reconciles with the fee schedule — the greater of the AIRPORT zone-class fee (SGD 6.00) and the RYDE_X vehicle-tier fee (SGD 4.00).

EVIDENCE QUALITY. No POL-NS-08 defect was found: the arrival tap matches a trace fix exactly (no clock skew), there are no sampling gaps, the chat is complete at 3 messages matching trip_record.chat_message_count, and the fare line reconciles. The deciding facts are carried by artifacts at weight 1.0, so the confidence cap is 1.0. The rider_track (67 fixes, all within 20.23 m of the pin) confirms the rider was at the pickup point; it is noted, though the refund does not depend on it.

The rider's suggestion that the driver sought a surcharge or took her for a tourist is not supported by the chat log, which contains no such demand — the driver's message stated the app's wait rule. No adverse finding is made on that point.
referrals: POL-NS-05(ii): record TRP-00614 as a false-arrival event against driver DRV-31422, the 'arrived' marker at 16:14:40 having been struck while no qualifying in-geofence fix exists anywhere in the trip.

ruling.explanation:
Rider, you are refunded the whole contested SGD 6.00 cancellation fee. Driver, no compensation is payable to you, and the trip is referred for a false-arrival record.

A no-show fee is chargeable only if all four conditions in POL-NS-01 hold, and three of them fail here. (a) holds: the trip record does contain an 'arrived' event at 16:14:40. (b) fails: the GPS trace's 79 driver fixes never come nearer than 881.64 m to the T4 pickup pin (mean 951.64 m, maximum 1,467.21 m) against the 150 m arrival radius the fee schedule sets for the AIRPORT zone class, and the derived arrival block records 0 qualifying in-radius fixes. (c) fails: the longest continuous in-geofence run is 0.0 seconds against the 480-second AIRPORT minimum. (d) fails: the trip was terminated by the rider at 16:23:40 with reason code RIDER_CHANGED_MIND, which is not one of the three codes limb (d) recognises, and no boarding event is recorded.

Because the driver was more than 300 m from the pin at the 16:14:40 'arrived' timestamp, that marker is FALSE under POL-NS-05. Recomputing the waiting clock from the first qualifying in-geofence fix, there is no qualifying in-geofence fix anywhere in the trip, so POL-NS-05(ii) applies: the SGD 6.00 is refunded in full, no driver compensation is payable, and a false-arrival record is directed in the referrals list. The driver's explanation that he pressed 'arrived' so the rider would know he was near does not change this — the marker is tested against the trace, not against intent. His account of waiting in the holding area does not engage POL-NS-03 either: that clause reaches only a driver stationary outside the arrival radius but within 400 m of the pin, and the trace places him between 881.64 m and 1,467.21 m throughout. The chat log is consistent with that: asked at 16:15:40 'where are you? I'm at the T4 pickup door', the driver answered 'not yet' at 16:16:20, a minute and forty seconds after marking arrival.

The rider's separate assertion that the driver 'wanted a surcharge and thought I was a tourist' is not supported by the record: the chat log is complete and unredacted at three messages, matching the trip record's chat_message_count of 3, and the driver's only substantive line — 'if wait too long app charge you not me' — states the platform's own wait rule. That element of the claim is set aside; it carries nothing.

Neither rider-contact exoneration nor escalation is engaged. POL-NS-04 does not apply because the driver replied within 120 seconds (rider 16:15:40, driver 16:16:20), a point both sides accepted. The POL-NS-07 anti-farming check does not trip: 2 no-show terminations in 30 days against 95 completed trips is a ratio of 0.021, below the 0.08 gate, and both limbs are required. No POL-NS-08 limb is breached — the arrived timestamp falls on the 10-second fix cadence, the trace has no gaps and 79 fixes, the chat log is complete, and the fee reconciles — so the apparent conflict between the trip record's arrival event and the trace is resolved by POL-NS-05 and nothing escalates.

The money figures: the fare breakdown records a SGD 6.00 cancellation fee, SGD 0.00 of it already refunded. The resolution rule takes the greater of the AIRPORT zone-class fee (SGD 6.00) and the RYDE_X vehicle-tier fee (SGD 4.00), which is SGD 6.00 and matches the ledger, so there is no amount defect. The refund is the SGD 6.00 cancellation-fee line.

The GPS trace, trip record, chat log and fare breakdown each carry weight 1.0, and the deciding facts — that the driver never entered the arrival geofence and never began the required hold — rest on them, so confidence is not discounted. The only below-weight artifact in the bundle is EV-ADVIS-00614-01 at weight 0.0, which is MISSING and carries no fact: it makes POL-NS-06(i) dwell accumulation unavailable, but there are no in-geofence intervals to accumulate, so it does not affect the outcome.

ruling.explanation:
Both parties: this is the SGD 6.00 cancellation fee charged on trip TRP-00614, a Changi Airport Terminal 4 (AIRPORT zone class) pickup. The charge does not stand.

For a no-show fee to be chargeable, POL-NS-01 requires all four of its conditions together, and three of them fail on the record. It is true that the trip record carries a driver 'arrived' event at 16:14:40, so limb (a) is met — but that alone carries nothing. ruling.explanation:
To both parties: the only question here is whether the SGD 6.00 cancellation fee was chargeable at all, and it was not.

POL-NS-01 sets four conditions and all four must hold. Only limb (a) holds — the trip record does carry an 'arrived' event at 16:14:40. Limb (b) fails on the driver's own telemetry: across all 79 fixes his closest approach to the T4 pickup pin is 881.64 m, with 0 fixes inside the 150 m arrival radius that applies to an AIRPORT pickup, so he was never inside the pickup geofence at or before the marker. Limb (c) fails: the longest continuous in-geofence run is 0 seconds against the 480-second AIRPORT minimum. Limb (d) fails: the trip was cancelled by the rider with reason code RIDER_CHANGED_MIND, which is none of the three codes limb (d) recognises (RIDER_NO_SHOW, RIDER_UNREACHABLE, EXCESSIVE_WAIT), and no boarding was recorded. Three of four limbs fail, so the fee is not chargeable under POL-NS-01.

Three clauses then give the rider the whole SGD 6.00. POL-NS-02: with no qualifying in-radius fix anywhere in the 15 minutes before cancellation, the driver never arrived and the cancellation fee is refunded in full. POL-NS-05: the 16:14:40 marker is FALSE, because at that timestamp the driver was more than 300 m from the pin; on the recomputed basis no qualifying in-geofence fix exists anywhere in the trip, so POL-NS-05(ii) refunds the fee in full, pays no compensation, and records the trip as a false-arrival event — that is the referral above. POL-NS-06: the effective dwell of 0 seconds falls 480 seconds short of the 480-second AIRPORT minimum, so the fee is not chargeable and is refunded in full, with no driver compensation payable.

The driver's points are answered. Limb (a) is satisfied — accepted, but limb (a) alone does not make the fee chargeable, and the other three limbs are broken. The amount is correct: SGD 6.00 is the greater of the AIRPORT zone-class fee (SGD 6.00) and the RYDE_X vehicle-tier fee (SGD 4.00), exactly matching the fare_breakdown cancellation-fee line, so no POL-NS-08(d) defect exists — accepted, and it makes no difference because the refund is a chargeability failure, not an arithmetic one. POL-NS-04 does not exonerate the rider (the driver replied 40 seconds after her message, inside the 120-second window) — accepted; the refund does not rest on POL-NS-04, so this changes nothing. The anti-farming check does not trip (2 no-show terminations against 95 completed trips, 0.021 against a 0.08 gate) — accepted; no escalation under POL-NS-09(d), and driver compensation is withheld for the independent reasons POL-NS-05(ii) and POL-NS-06 give, namely that POL-NS-01 is not satisfied at all. The rider's assertion that the driver 'wanted a surcharge and thought I was a tourist' is rejected as unsupported: the chat log is complete and unredacted at 3 messages, matching trip_record.chat_message_count, and contains no such demand — his only substantive line states the app's wait rule.

The driver's statement that he waited in the 'holding area' and pressed arrived so the rider would know he was near is taken into account but does not change the outcome. POL-NS-03 requires the driver to have been stationary outside the arrival radius but within 400 m of the pin; the trace places him between 881.64 m and 1,467.21 m away throughout the entire attempt, outside that ceiling, so POL-NS-03 is not engaged and does not displace the refund. A 'holding area' sub-location is in any case not corroborated by any venue_id or by anything in the chat log.

On confidence and weight: the deciding facts — that the driver never entered the pickup geofence, that the dwell was 0 seconds, and that the marker was struck from over 300 m away — rest on the GPS trace and the trip record, each at weight_multiplier 1.0, and are corroborated by the chat log (weight 1.0), in which the driver answers 'not yet' a minute and forty seconds after pressing arrived. No artifact deciding this case is impaired under POL-NS-08(a) to (d): no clock skew (the arrival timestamp coincides with a fix), no trace gap (0-second maximum gap, 79 fixes, 100% coverage, rider track present), no chat defect (3 messages as recorded), and no fare defect. EV-ADVIS-00614-01 is MISSING at weight 0.0, but it carries none of the deciding facts — it would matter only to accumulating separate dwell intervals under POL-NS-06(i), which is irrelevant when there was no in-geofence interval at all. No POL-NS-09 escalation trigger fires: confidence is above the 0.70 floor, POL-NS-05 resolves the apparent conflict between the trip record's arrival marker and the trace rather than leaving it unresolved, and the counterparty-dispute and abuse counters are all below their gates.
referrals: POL-NS-05(ii) — record this trip as a false-arrival event against driver DRV-31422: the 'arrived' marker struck at 16:14:40 was set while the driver's trace placed him more than 300 m from the pickup pin (closest approach 881.64 m on the whole trip), and no qualifying in-geofence fix exists anywhere in the trip.

The derived driver track never comes closer than 881.64 m to the T4 pickup pin across 79 fixes, while the derived arrival block records 0 qualifying in-radius fixes against the 150 m arrival radius that the fee_schedule sets for the AIRPORT zone class. A driver who never entered the arrival radius did not arrive at the pickup point.

The longest continuous in-geofence run in the derived arrival block is 0.0 seconds, measured from the (non-existent) first qualifying in-geofence fix, against a required continuous dwell of 480 seconds for an AIRPORT pickup. The required hold was never begun, let alone completed.

Limb (d) fails on the trip record's own terms. The trip was cancelled by the rider with cancellation_reason_code RIDER_CHANGED_MIND, which is none of the three codes limb (d) recognises (RIDER_NO_SHOW, RIDER_UNREACHABLE, EXCESSIVE_WAIT), and the record shows no boarding event. Three of the four POL-NS-01 conditions therefore fail, and the fee is not chargeable under this clause.

The 'arrived' marker struck at 16:14:40 is FALSE under POL-NS-05: at the arrival timestamp the driver's trace places him more than 300 m from the pickup pin — his closest approach on the entire trip is 881.64 m, so he was more than 300 m away at every instant of the attempt. Because no qualifying in-geofence fix exists anywhere in the trip, POL-NS-05(ii) applies: the cancellation fee is refunded in full, no driver compensation is payable, and the trip should be recorded as a false-arrival event in the ruling's referrals list.

A driver who answers 'not yet' has not arrived; POL-NS-02 is not satisfied and the contested SGD 6.00 is refundable in full. The fare line itself reconciles at SGD 6.00 (the greater of the AIRPORT zone-class fee and the RYDE_X tier fee), so this is a chargeability failure, not an arithmetic one, and the refund is the whole SGD 6.00.

ledger.claim: The driver's 'holding area' account does not turn this into a wrong-entrance case. POL-NS-03 applies only where the driver was stationary outside the arrival radius but within 400 m of the pickup pin; his own trace places him between 881.64 m and 1,467.21 m away throughout the attempt, outside that ceiling, so POL-NS-03 is not engaged at all and nothing in it displaces the full refund that POL-NS-02 and POL-NS-06 give the rider.

No driver compensation can be ordered on these facts. POL-NS-07 pays only where POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full and no clause from POL-NS-03 to POL-NS-06 displaces it; here POL-NS-01 fails on limbs (b), (c) and (d), and POL-NS-05 and POL-NS-06 displace it and state in terms that no compensation is payable. There is accordingly no driver-side cost for the rider to fund and no basis for leaving the charge in place.

The rider was at the pin and coordinating, not absent: the rider track holds 67 fixes all within 20.23 m of the pickup pin, well inside the 200 m AIRPORT rider-presence radius, and she wrote 'where are you? I'm at the T4 pickup door'. I do not rely on POL-NS-04 for the refund — its limb (b) is not met, because the driver did reply in the chat within 120 seconds (rider's message 16:15:40, driver's reply 16:16:20) — and I say so rather than stretch it. The refund rests on POL-NS-02, POL-NS-05 and POL-NS-06, none of which depends on the rider's conduct.

The trip record contains a driver 'arrived' event for this trip at 16:14:40, so limb (a) of POL-NS-01 - the requirement that the trip_record contain an 'arrived' event for the trip - is satisfied on the face of the record.

The cancellation fee the ledger actually took is the correct figure for this trip and cannot be impeached on amount: this is an AIRPORT zone-class pickup, the zone-class fee is SGD 6.00 and the RYDE_X vehicle-tier fee is SGD 4.00, and the greater of the two under the fee_schedule resolution rule - SGD 6.00 - is exactly what fare_breakdown.cancellation_fee records, so there is no POL-NS-08(d) fare defect available to the rider.

POL-NS-04 cannot exonerate the rider: her locating message ('where are you? I'm at the T4 pickup door') was sent at 16:15:40 and the driver posted a reply at 16:16:20, forty seconds later and well inside the 120-second window, so limb (b) of POL-NS-04 fails and that rider-exonerating route is closed on the chat log itself.

There is no fee-farming pattern to hold against the driver, and the anti-farming check under POL-NS-07 does not trip: driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 2 and driver_profile.completed_trips_30d is 95, a ratio of 0.021 against a 0.08 gate, and both limbs of that test are required.

The rider's assertion that the driver 'wanted a surcharge and thought I was a tourist' is not supported anywhere in the record: the chat log is complete and unredacted at three messages, matching trip_record.chat_message_count of 3, and the driver's only substantive line - 'if wait too long app charge you not me' - states the platform's own wait rule rather than demanding anything, so that element of the claim is unsupported and cannot carry an adverse finding under POL-GEN-03.
